recommendation.recommendation: Implement immediate flood irrigation combined with rapid field scouting and organic soil amendment to alleviate severe water stress and vegetation decline.
recommendation.justification: Satellite data shows critical canopy loss (NDVI 0.154) and extreme water stress (NDWI -0.204) while weather, soil pH and nitrogen are optimal. Immediate water delivery and early disease/nutrient diagnosis are required to prevent irreversible yield loss, and the farm benefits from strong market prices.
actions: 1. Conduct a thorough field inspection within the next 12 hours to identify symptoms of Fusarium wilt, Verticillium wilt, aphids, or bollworms and note any nutrient deficiency signs.
2. Activate flood irrigation immediately to bring soil moisture to field capacity; aim for a water depth of 5‑7 cm across the field and repeat every 7‑10 days until NDWI returns to ≥0.25.
3. Apply 5‑7 t ha⁻¹ of well‑composted organic manure (or green manure) to raise organic carbon levels and improve soil structure.
4. Install a light mulching layer (straw or shredded crop residue) after irrigation to reduce evaporation and protect soil surface.
5. If disease or pest presence is confirmed, treat with recommended fungicides (for wilt) and insecticides or biological controls (for aphids/bollworms) according to label rates.
6. Record irrigation volumes, soil moisture (using a handheld probe), and any pest/disease observations in a daily log.
recommendation.expected_outcome: Restored soil moisture will reduce water stress, improve NDVI to ≥0.4 within two weeks, and mitigate further canopy loss. Organic amendment will increase soil organic carbon, enhancing long‑term fertility and reducing erosion risk. Timely pest/disease control will prevent secondary yield losses, positioning the crop for a market‑grade harvest.
monitoring_plan: • Daily visual scouting for pest/disease symptoms for the next 14 days.
• Soil moisture checks at 20 cm depth every 2 days until NDWI stabilizes above 0.25.
• Satellite NDVI/NDWI analysis (or drone NDVI) weekly for the next 3 weeks.
• Record irrigation events and volumes; adjust frequency based on moisture readings.
• Re‑measure soil organic carbon (using a field kit) after 4 weeks to assess amendment impact.
• Track market price trends weekly to plan optimal harvest timing.

steps.finding: Implement immediate flood irrigation combined with rapid field scouting and organic soil amendment to alleviate severe water stress and vegetation decline.
actions: 1. Conduct a thorough field inspection within the next 12 hours to identify symptoms of Fusarium wilt, Verticillium wilt, aphids, or bollworms and note any nutrient deficiency signs.
2. Activate flood irrigation immediately to bring soil moisture to field capacity; aim for a water depth of 5‑7 cm across the field and repeat every 7‑10 days until NDWI returns to ≥0.25.
3. Apply 5‑7 t ha⁻¹ of well‑composted organic manure (or green manure) to raise organic carbon levels and improve soil structure.
4. Install a light mulching layer (straw or shredded crop residue) after irrigation to reduce evaporation and protect soil surface.
5. If disease or pest presence is confirmed, treat with recommended fungicides (for wilt) and insecticides or biological controls (for aphids/bollworms) according to label rates.
6. Record irrigation volumes, soil moisture (using a handheld probe), and any pest/disease observations in a daily log.
steps.justification: Satellite data shows critical canopy loss (NDVI 0.154) and extreme water stress (NDWI -0.204) while weather, soil pH and nitrogen are optimal. Immediate water delivery and early disease/nutrient diagnosis are required to prevent irreversible yield loss, and the farm benefits from strong market prices.
